Subject: Production: sudden 5xx and p95 spike on private cluster

Alex / Marissa —

We just saw a sudden jump in 5xx responses and p95 latency on our private VPC cluster starting ~07:55 PT. Affected endpoints: /generate and /chat-stream. Around 20% of requests are returning 503s and p95 has jumped from ~220ms to ~1.9s. This is customer-facing for two of our pilot customers and they're already noisy.

We've attached a hotpath dump and a short tail log excerpt (hotpath_dump_1109.log). Early looks show a pattern of concurrent requests triggering tokenization stalls and repeated KV cache misses. Can you triage immediately? Our CTO (cc'ed) wants a short exec update in 30–45 minutes.

Claire
Ops Lead, HelioPharm

Triage notes (initial, from the cluster metrics and the provided dump):

- Symptom: concurrent tail latency and 503s aligned with sudden increase in short L1 requests (many < 128 tokens) hitting a subset of hotshards.
- Root hypothesis: recent runtime kernel switch to quantized GEMM path + continuous-batching change exposed a regression in KV cache eviction policy. When eviction is aggressive under spike, we see repeated cache misses causing tokenizer stalls and backpressure, which cascades into queued requests and 503s.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low risk -> moderate):
A) Apply a temporary route-level concurrency cap (10 rps/core) — manual throttle via route policy (10–15 minutes to apply).
B) Disable the new quantized GEMM kernel on the affected pool (config_delta_rollback.patch) and restart the pool in a rolling fashion (can do canary on 10% of nodes first). Expected improvement: p95 down to ~300–450ms based on previous similar rollbacks.
C) Increase KV cache retention window from 30s -> 90s for hot prefixes to reduce eviction churn (config change).

I'll attach a small flamegraph (flamegraph_1109.svg) and a config diff with the rollback. If you approve A+B I can run the canary immediately and report within 12–18 minutes.

- Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Claire / Rajiv —

Appreciate the quick coordination. Short status & plan summary for execs before the bridge: 

What happened (short): a runtime kernel + batching change increased cache churn on a hot subset of shards; that drove tokenizer stalls and queued requests which produced 503s.

What we're doing now (minutes):
- 09:25 PT: route-level concurrency cap applied to /generate (10 rps/core) — immediate 5xx reduction observed in metrics (monitoring dashboard).
- 09:40 PT: rolled out rollback canary to 10% of nodes in the affected pool (config_delta_rollback.patch). Observed p95 drop from ~1.9s -> ~420ms on canary nodes.
- 09:58 PT: canary look-good window completed; we're proceeding with rolling rollback across remaining nodes with a 5-minute stagger per node. Expected full remediation in ~25–30 minutes.

Expected impact: throughput will be temporarily reduced while rollback completes; p95 should return to sub-500ms and 503 rate should drop to baseline. We'll keep the route-level throttle in place until the rollback is fully rolled out and metrics are stable for 5 mins.

Next steps for execs:
- I'll run a 15-min exec sync at 10:20 PT to confirm the rollback outcome and close the incident. If Rajiv wants a deeper postmortem, we'll schedule a 1:1 with Vivek and the runtime team after stabilization.
